questions.question: A vehicle's limited-slip differential (LSD) is experiencing a consistent 'clunking' noise and binding sensation that is present during tight, low-speed turns on dry pavement. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause binding or clunking in the LSD.
Low differential fluid will cause whining.
Worn components create clunking and binding.
Overheated rotors do not impact differential operation.
questions.explanation: Worn components in the LSD will cause a clunking sound and will prevent the LSD from operating properly, creating a binding sensation during low speed turns.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is exhibiting a complete lack of functionality, with a warning message on the dashboard that states 'Camera Obstructed' or 'System Unavailable'. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Obstructed camera view or faulty connection
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to lane keeping.
Radar sensors do not manage the LKA system.
Obstructed view or faulty camera connection will prevent operation.
Low battery voltage does not relate to the camera system.
questions.explanation: A camera obstruction or faulty connection will prevent the LKA system from working, and will illuminate a message on the dashboard.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is exhibiting a complete loss of assist, but only after extended periods of highway driving and then becomes difficult to steer during low-speed maneuvers. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause this.
Low fluid creates heavy steering not a complete loss.
Failing pumps will fail during extended use and low speeds.
Misaligned steering does not cause steering assist issues.
questions.explanation: A failing power steering pump will not have the ability to provide adequate assist after extended periods of use, and will cause a loss of power during low speed maneuvers.

questions.question: A vehicle's differential is experiencing a consistent 'humming' noise that is most prominent during highway driving, and will disappear during deceleration. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not relate to differential noises.
Low differential fluid will not create a highway specific humming sound.
Worn gears do not create a humming sound.
Damaged bearings will create a humming noise at highway speed.
questions.explanation: Damaged pinion gear bearings will create a humming sound during highway driving, but it will disappear when decelerating due to reduced load.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is exhibiting an inconsistent response, sometimes activating too early, and sometimes too late, and a system warning light illuminates intermittently. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn brake pads do not cause an inconsistent response.
Faulty yaw rate sensors cause inconsistent responses.
Misaligned steering does not cause inconsistent ESC.
Low tire pressure does not cause inconsistent response from ESC.
questions.explanation: A faulty yaw rate sensor will cause the system to have an inconsistent and delayed response, and can cause the system warning light to illuminate intermittently.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is exhibiting a complete failure on all wheels, and also causes a reduction in the braking performance of all wheels, and the warning light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to ABS.
Radar sensors do not relate to braking.
A faulty control module will cause full failure.
Worn brake pads will reduce braking performance.
questions.explanation: A faulty ABS control module will cause a complete failure of the system and will also illuminate the warning light and prevent the system from modulating pressure which will reduce braking performance.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a complete lack of power, very rough idle, and frequent stalling, a strong smell of unburnt fuel and excessive black smoke from the exhaust and the check engine light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Clogged air filters create rich conditions.
Leaking intake gaskets cause lean conditions.
Faulty fuel injectors cause all of the mentioned symptoms.
Worn spark plugs do not cause all of these symptoms.
questions.explanation: Faulty fuel injectors can cause all the mentioned issues including a complete lack of power, rough idling, frequent stalling, fuel smells and excessive black smoke, and will also illuminate the check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is exhibiting a tendency to inconsistently adjust the speed, surging and slowing, and overreacting to small changes in the distance to the vehicle ahead and the warning light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not impact speed control.
Misaligned sensors create inconsistent speed adjustments.
Dirty sensors create inconsistent speed adjustments.
Faulty control modules create inconsistent adjustments.
questions.explanation: A misaligned or dirty sensor or a faulty control module can cause inconsistent operation that includes surging and slowing and over reacting to distance changes and will also illuminate the warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is exhibiting completely incorrect and very inconsistent pressure readings with some sensors showing very high pressure, and others showing extremely low pressure, and the warning light is on. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Faulty TPMS sensor in the wheel
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to TPMS.
Radar sensors do not relate to TPMS.
Low battery voltage will not cause high or low readings.
Faulty sensors cause inconsistent and incorrect data.
questions.explanation: A faulty sensor in one or more tires will cause the system to report incorrect data, and cause inconsistent readings with some reading high and some low and also will illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is exhibiting a complete lack of cooling, reduced airflow, a burning plastic or electrical odor, and a consistent loud squealing sound from the compressor. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Blocked expansion valve or orifice tube
feedbacks: Cabin filters do not cause electrical or squealing noises.
Low refrigerant does not cause electrical odors.
Faulty compressors can produce all these symptoms.
A blocked valve or tube does not cause electrical smells or squealing.
questions.explanation: A faulty A/C compressor will not be able to create cooling, will cause a reduction in airflow, will make a squealing sound and when faulty can create a burning plastic odor.

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery pack is exhibiting a significantly reduced range, significantly reduced charging rate and is producing excessive heat during normal driving and when charging. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Internal cell degradation and increased resistance
feedbacks: Slow charging will not cause all these issues.
Increased resistance will cause these symptoms.
Overcharging degrades the cells not cause these specific issues.
Ideal conditions do not cause degradation or overheating.
questions.explanation: Internal cell degradation increases resistance and will cause a reduced range, slow charging speeds and excessive heat generation, especially during driving and charging.

questions.question: A vehicle's limited-slip differential (LSD) is experiencing a loud and consistent 'grinding' noise, a binding sensation, and reduced effectiveness when turning on dry pavement, especially when accelerating. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Worn LSD clutch packs or gears
feedbacks: Worn tires do not create a grinding sound in the LSD.
Low differential fluid will cause a whining.
Worn components can create grinding and binding during operation.
Overheated rotors do not impact the LSD system.
questions.explanation: Worn components in the LSD will not engage properly and will create grinding noises, a binding sensation, and a reduction in its ability to transfer power, especially when accelerating and turning on dry pavement.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is exhibiting erratic behavior, frequently activating when there are no lane markings and also sometimes not activating when it is required to, with a system warning light that will intermittently illuminate. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not impact lane keep behavior.
Radar sensors do not manage the LKA system.
A faulty camera or connection causes erratic operation.
Low battery voltage will not cause erratic operation of LKA.
questions.explanation: A faulty camera sensor or connection will cause the system to operate erratically and sometimes not at all, and will cause an intermittent system warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is exhibiting a complete loss of assist only when turning to one side, and also accompanied by a grinding noise during turns. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause one sided steering issues.
Low fluid creates heavy steering.
Faulty rack will cause binding and grinding.
Misaligned steering causes pulling not power assist issues.
questions.explanation: A faulty steering rack will not operate properly and will cause a complete loss of assist only when turning one direction and may also create grinding noises during operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's differential is experiencing a consistent 'humming' noise that is most noticeable during acceleration and deceleration, and will completely disappear during consistent cruising speeds. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause differential humming.
Low differential fluid will cause whining not humming.
Worn gears do not create a humming noise.
Damaged bearings cause humming that disappears at cruise.
questions.explanation: Damaged pinion gear bearings will create a humming noise that will be most noticeable during acceleration and deceleration, but will disappear during consistent cruising speeds due to the constant load and rotation.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is exhibiting inconsistent and delayed activation, sometimes engaging correctly but other times either too late or not at all, and a system warning light illuminates intermittently. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn brake pads do not cause inconsistent activation.
Faulty yaw rate sensors will cause inconsistent and delayed activation.
Misaligned steering does not impact the ESC response time.
Low tire pressure does not impact the system response time.
questions.explanation: A faulty yaw rate sensor will cause the system to have erratic and delayed responses and can cause the system warning light to illuminate intermittently.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is exhibiting a complete failure and also is causing a complete lack of braking performance on all wheels with the system warning light illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to ABS functionality.
Radar sensors do not relate to ABS functionality.
A faulty ABS control module will cause a full system failure.
Worn brake pads will reduce overall braking performance not prevent it completely.
questions.explanation: A faulty ABS control module will prevent the entire system from functioning, and will also prevent braking functionality as well as illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a complete lack of power, frequent stalling, rough idle, no acceleration above idle, a strong fuel smell, and black smoke, and the check engine light is illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Clogged air filters cause a rich condition.
Leaking intake manifold gaskets cause a lean condition.
Faulty fuel injectors cause a rich condition, stalling, no RPMs, fuel smell and black smoke.
Worn spark plugs cause misfires.
questions.explanation: Faulty fuel injectors can cause all of these symptoms, including a lack of power, stalling, rough idles, a fuel smell, and black smoke, and will also illuminate the check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is exhibiting erratic and unsafe behavior, including a tendency to rapidly accelerate then suddenly and aggressively brake, and also frequently losing track of the vehicle ahead and the system warning light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not impact ACC acceleration.
Misaligned radar sensors cause erratic performance.
Dirty radar sensors cause reduced performance.
A faulty control module can cause all these issues.
questions.explanation: A misaligned or dirty sensor, or a faulty control module can cause a variety of unsafe behavior patterns, including sudden accelerations and decelerations, losing track of vehicles ahead, and illuminate the warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is exhibiting completely incorrect and unreliable data with no sensors registering correctly, and a consistent warning light that remains on at all times, and is also not communicating with the vehicles onboard computer. What is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to TPMS operation.
Radar sensors do not relate to TPMS operation.
Low battery voltage can reduce sensor performance.
A faulty receiver will prevent communication to the computer.
questions.explanation: A faulty TPMS receiver module will prevent the entire system from operating, will cause completely incorrect data, will illuminate the warning light and will also prevent the computer from communicating with the system.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is exhibiting a complete lack of cooling, airflow, all components not operating, a persistent burning electrical smell, and also a rattling sound coming from under the dashboard. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Faulty A/C compressor clutch or control
Faulty blower motor resistor or module
feedbacks: Cabin filters do not cause a lack of cooling, airflow, electrical odors and rattling.
Low refrigerant will not prevent system engagement or cause electrical odors and rattling.
A faulty compressor will not produce all the listed symptoms.
Faulty blower controls can cause a lack of airflow, electrical odors, and the rattling sounds.
questions.explanation: A faulty blower motor control module or resistor will prevent airflow from occurring, it can create a burning electrical smell, and also can create a rattling sound, but will not prevent the compressor from working.

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery pack is exhibiting an extremely rapid decrease in driving range, very slow charging times, a rapid and consistent increase in temperature during charging and normal driving, frequent and severe cell voltage imbalances and also exhibits signs of rapid swelling in the pack. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Internal cell short circuits and damage
feedbacks: Slow charging does not cause any of these issues.
Internal cell shorts cause all of the issues mentioned.
Overcharging does not create swelling or cell imbalance.
Ideal conditions do not cause any degradation in performance.
questions.explanation: Internal cell shorts will cause a rapid loss in range, a significantly reduced charging rate, high temperatures, cell voltage imbalances and rapid swelling due to out gassing.

questions.question: A vehicle's limited-slip differential (LSD) is exhibiting a consistent 'grinding' noise, significant binding during turns, frequent clicking or popping noises and a reduction in performance when accelerating on loose surfaces. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Severely worn or damaged LSD clutch packs and gears
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause LSD issues.
Low differential fluid causes whining.
Worn or damaged components will cause all the mentioned symptoms.
Overheated rotors do not impact the LSD.
questions.explanation: Severely worn or damaged LSD components including gears and clutch packs will cause significant issues during normal operation, including grinding, binding, clicking or popping noises, and a significant reduction in performance especially on low grip surfaces.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is exhibiting a complete lack of functionality with the warning message 'System Unavailable, Steering Assistance Disabled', a warning light on the dashboard, and the system failing to activate even when lane markings are clearly visible. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the camera and its associated wiring and control systems
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not prevent system operation.
Radar sensors do not relate to lane keeping systems.
Complete camera failure or wiring issues will cause a system failure.
Low battery voltage does not cause a complete system failure.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the camera and its associated wiring or control systems will cause the system to completely fail and illuminate the warning message.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is exhibiting a complete loss of power assist, a loud grinding noise, significant stiffness in the steering, and also a noticeable resistance when turning the wheel, only when turning to one side, and especially noticeable during parking maneuvers. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the steering rack internals
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause the listed issues.
Low power steering fluid will cause heavy steering.
A rack failure will cause all the mentioned issues.
Misaligned steering will not cause all the mentioned issues.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the steering rack internals will not operate correctly and will result in a complete loss of assist when turning to only one side, will create a grinding noise, and significant resistance, especially during low speed operation and parking maneuvers.

questions.question: A vehicle's differential is exhibiting a consistent 'whining' noise during operation, which will rapidly become a 'howling' noise during acceleration, and a consistent 'grinding' noise during deceleration, and will also exhibit a clunking noise when turning sharply, and is producing metallic flakes in the differential fluid when changed. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Severe damage to the differential gears and bearings
feedbacks: Worn tires do not relate to differential noises.
Low differential fluid will not cause all the listed symptoms.
Severely worn gears and bearings will cause all of the listed issues.
Overheated rotors do not relate to the differential.
questions.explanation: Severe damage to the differential gears and bearings will cause a variety of issues including whining noises during normal operation, howling during acceleration, grinding during deceleration, clunking when turning, and will also produce metallic flakes in the fluid due to the material breaking down.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is exhibiting a complete lack of activation, a system warning light that is constantly on, a noticeable pulling sensation towards one side when cornering and a reduction in braking effectiveness of only one side of the vehicle. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: A complete failure of the ABS and Yaw Rate Sensor
feedbacks: Worn brake pads will only reduce braking performance not cause system failure.
Faulty yaw rate sensors do not cause only one side to perform poorly.
Complete system failure will cause the issues mentioned.
Low tire pressure does not relate to complete system failure.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the ABS and Yaw Rate sensors will prevent proper stability control operation and will result in a complete failure of the ESC system, including a pull to one side during cornering due to uneven braking and will illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is exhibiting a complete failure, along with a complete lack of braking on all wheels, a system warning light is on, a complete lack of engagement of the EBD system and a noticeable pulling sensation to one side, and the vehicle will not start with the ABS system connected. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the ABS Control Module
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to braking performance.
Radar sensors do not relate to braking performance.
A faulty ABS control module causes a complete system failure.
Worn brake pads do not prevent the system from working.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the ABS control module will prevent all of the system operations, and will also cause the entire system to be inoperable, which will also cause a lack of braking, and will prevent the car from starting and illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a complete lack of power, frequent stalling, a very rough idle, a strong smell of unburnt fuel, significant black smoke, and also a loud backfiring sound when the engine is turned off and a check engine light is illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the fuel injection system
feedbacks: Clogged air filters cause a rich condition.
Leaking intake gaskets cause a lean condition.
A complete failure will cause all of the listed symptoms.
Worn spark plugs cause misfires.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the fuel injection system will cause all of the listed symptoms including a lack of power, frequent stalling, a rough idle, a strong fuel smell, black smoke, and also backfiring, and will illuminate the check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is experiencing frequent and unwarranted braking events on curved roads. This is most likely due to a failure in which system?
feedbacks: Radar sensors primarily detect distance and speed, not curvature.
Lidar sensors are used for high definition mapping and object detection but not specifically curvature
Steering angle sensors provide information about steering wheel position but does not infer road curvature
Lateral acceleration sensors measure the force experienced during turning, allowing the system to differentiate a turn versus a possible accident.
questions.explanation: Lateral acceleration sensors are the most likely culprit when ACC causes frequent braking events on curved roads because it measures force experienced during a turn allowing the system to differenciate a turn from a possible accident

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery management system (BMS) is reporting an imbalance in cell voltages during charging. What could be a potential cause for this?
feedbacks: A faulty charger would cause issues in the whole charging system not specifically cell imbalance.
Temperature variation between cells can lead to internal resistance differences, therefore causing cell imbalance.
Coolant is important for thermal management, not cell imbalance.
Overcharging can cause multiple failures but not specifically cell voltage imbalance.
questions.explanation: Temperature differences create variance in cell internal resistance, resulting in imbalance of voltages.

questions.question: A gasoline engine experiences significant pre-ignition (knock). Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Low octane fuel causes detonation not pre-ignition.
Rich air-fuel mixture will not cause pre-ignition.
Excessive spark advance is a primary cause of pre-ignition.
Leaking intake valve would not cause pre-ignition
questions.explanation: Excessive spark advance causes the mixture to ignite too early, creating knock.

questions.question: During a crash test, a vehicle's side impact airbags fail to deploy. Which sensor is MOST crucial for proper side airbag deployment?
feedbacks: Frontal impact sensors activate the frontal airbags.
Side impact pressure sensors are designed to activate side airbags on impact.
Yaw rate sensors measure rotation but are not necessary for side airbag deployment.
Wheel speed sensors measure rotational speed.
questions.explanation: Side impact pressure sensors are placed in the doors and side structures to detect an impact and trigger the side airbag.

questions.question: A vehicle's CAN bus is experiencing intermittent communication errors. What is a common cause of such an issue?
feedbacks: Low battery voltage causes various problems, but specifically intermittent CAN bus issues.
Incorrect CAN bus termination resistors are common causes of intermittent CAN bus communication.
Faulty ECU can cause various issues but not specifically intermittent CAN bus errors.
Overheated Transmission Control Module would cause Transmission specific errors not CAN bus errors.
questions.explanation: Improper CAN bus termination resistors will create signal reflection that leads to communication errors.

questions.question: A vehicle's steering system exhibits excessive play (looseness). What is a likely mechanical cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause steering play.
Tie rod ends connect steering to the wheels, and when loose will result in excessive play.
Worn brake rotors do not cause steering play.
Incorrect wheel alignment can cause handling issues, not steering play.
questions.explanation: Loose tie rod ends will result in a loose or undefined feel to the steering response.

questions.question: A vehicle's hybrid system is showing reduced regenerative braking efficiency. Which component is the MOST likely source of the problem?
feedbacks: Inverter changes DC to AC, not a likely cause of reduced regen.
Battery packs hold the charge, so reduced efficiency is not a cause.
The electric motor is responsible for both generating and propulsion, so this is the most likely cause.
Transmission transmits mechanical power and would not affect regenerative braking.
questions.explanation: The electric motor generator is responsible for both propulsion and regenerative braking, and is most likely the cause when regen efficiency is reduced.

questions.question: A vehicle with a direct injection gasoline engine is experiencing carbon buildup on the intake valves. Which is the most effective solution?
feedbacks: Fuel system cleaner does not clean the intake valves in DI engines.
Direct mechanical cleaning of the intake valves is the most effective solution.
High octane fuel does not mitigate the cause of carbon buildup.
Engine oil additives do not remove carbon buildup on intake valves.
questions.explanation: Direct injection does not allow fuel/cleaner to clean the intake valves, therefore a cleaning service is required.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is activating excessively, even during normal driving. What could be a potential cause?
feedbacks: Incorrect tire pressure can cause vehicle instability and trigger ESC.
Faulty wheel speed sensors can provide inaccurate data, causing ESC to trigger even if it is not needed.
Worn brake pads don't cause ESC issues.
Engine misfires will not cause ESC issues.
questions.explanation: Faulty wheel speed sensors would provide inaccurate data causing ESC to activate without needing to.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic transmission is experiencing rough shifts and slippage. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Worn clutch plates in the differential
feedbacks: Worn engine mounts cause engine vibrations, not transmission slippage.
Low transmission fluid level will cause rough shifts and slippage.
Faulty ABS sensors do not cause transmission issues.
Differential does not cause transmission issues.
questions.explanation: Low transmission fluid will prevent adequate pressure and lubrication, which leads to slippage and rough shifts.

questions.question: A vehicle's radar-based blind spot monitoring system is giving false alarms, particularly in heavy rain. What is the most likely cause?
answers: Radar sensor is being blocked by debris
Signal reflection due to heavy rain
feedbacks: While faulty radar sensor is a possibility, rain can cause issues with radar based systems
Misaligned radar sensors will not cause false alarms only in heavy rain.
Debris would cause false alarms at all times, not just in the rain
Heavy rain can reflect radar signals, causing the system to falsely detect objects.
questions.explanation: Heavy rain will create signal reflection that can lead to the radar sensing multiple non existent objects.

questions.question: A vehicle's thermal management system for the battery pack is experiencing reduced performance. Which component is the MOST likely source of the problem?
feedbacks: Coolant pumps keep the coolant flow moving. Faulty pumps would reduce performance.
Cabin heater does not manage battery pack temperature.
HVAC compressor does not manage battery pack temperature.
Battery control module monitors, not manage temperature directly.
questions.explanation: Coolant pumps move the coolant that transfers heat from the battery to the radiator, a faulty pump would cause reduced performance.

questions.question: A high-performance vehicle exhibits excessive understeer during cornering. What is the MOST likely cause related to chassis setup?
feedbacks: Stiff rear sway bar promotes oversteer.
Stiff front sway bar will cause excessive understeer.
High rear tire pressure promotes oversteer.
Low front tire pressure promotes oversteer.
questions.explanation: Stiff front sway bar transfers more load to the front, making the front tires lose grip and therefore promoting understeer.

questions.question: A diesel engine is emitting excessive black smoke. What is the most likely reason?
feedbacks: Exhaust manifold leaks would not cause black smoke.
Faulty injectors will cause overfueling which leads to black smoke.
Clogged air filters cause a lean condition, and not black smoke.
Low compression does not cause black smoke.
questions.explanation: Faulty injectors can cause overfueling which leads to excess unburnt fuel.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is activating erratically during normal braking. Which sensor could be the cause?
feedbacks: Steering angle sensor provides data for steering, not braking.
Brake pressure sensor does not directly control ABS activation.
Erratic wheel speed sensors will cause ABS to engage when unnecessary.
Yaw rate sensor measure rotation, not braking.
questions.explanation: Erratic wheel speed sensor data will cause the ABS system to think the wheels are locking up when they are not.

questions.question: A vehicle's transmission control module (TCM) is reporting a solenoid fault code. What is the function of solenoids in an automatic transmission?
feedbacks: Solenoids don't measure fluid temp.
Solenoids are electrical valves that direct hydraulic pressure, therefore control gear shifting.
Solenoids don't control engine timing.
Solenoids don't regulate brake force.
questions.explanation: Solenoids are used in automatic transmissions to control gear shifting by controlling the flow of hydraulic pressure to clutches or brakes inside the transmission.

questions.question: A vehicle's electric power steering (EPS) system is becoming stiff or difficult to turn intermittently. Which could be a potential cause?
answers: Weak electrical connection to the EPS motor
feedbacks: Low tire pressure can cause difficulty in steering but not intermittent.
A faulty steering sensor would not cause stiffness, rather no steering.
A weak electrical connection can cause intermittent stiffness in electric power steering.
Worn steering rack will cause play or looseness, not intermittent stiffness.
questions.explanation: A poor electrical connection causes the EPS system to intermittently stop working or not operate at 100%.

questions.question: A vehicle with a continuously variable transmission (CVT) is experiencing belt slippage. Which is a potential mechanical reason?
answers: Worn clutch pack in the differential
feedbacks: Worn engine mounts don't cause slippage.
Low transmission fluid causes slippage in all types of transmissions.
Overheated brake rotors do not cause transmission slippage.
Differential does not cause CVT slippage.
questions.explanation: Low transmission fluid causes a lack of hydraulic pressure on the belt resulting in slippage.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane departure warning (LDW) system is frequently triggered on straight roads, even when the vehicle is centered in the lane. What could be the most likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors measure steering input not vehicle position in a lane
Misaligned camera sensor or poor calibration will cause the LDW to malfunction.
Incorrect tire pressure has no direct correlation with lane assist.
Weak battery has no direct correlation with lane assist
questions.explanation: Misaligned camera sensors or poor calibration will give the LDW a false view of the lane markings.

questions.question: A vehicle's active suspension system is exhibiting inconsistent damping performance. What could be the most likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires don't affect damping.
Faulty air compressor does not affect damping specifically.
Faulty damping actuators directly affect damping by controlling the valve within the shock.
Misaligned steering does not affect damping.
questions.explanation: Damping actuators control the valves within the shock to vary damping force.

questions.question: A lithium-ion battery pack is experiencing rapid capacity degradation. What is the MOST likely cause related to charging behavior?
feedbacks: Slow charging is typically good for battery health.
Frequent deep discharges can degrade lithium-ion battery capacity.
Low ambient temperature charging does not cause capacity degradation, but can cause damage.
Overcharging degrades a batteries cells rapidly.
questions.explanation: Both frequent deep discharges and overcharging contribute significantly to capacity degradation in lithium-ion batteries.

questions.question: A turbocharged gasoline engine is experiencing a sudden loss of boost pressure. What is the most likely cause?
answers: Boost leak in the intake system
feedbacks: Oxygen sensor does not manage boost pressure.
Boost leaks are the most common issue when boost pressure is suddenly lost.
Clogged catalytic converter affects exhaust flow not boost pressure.
Dirty air filter does not directly cause boost loss.
questions.explanation: Leaks in the intake system cause loss of pressure by releasing compressed air.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is struggling to maintain the vehicle's position in the center of the lane during low-light conditions. What is a potential cause?
answers: Poor camera visibility due to low light
feedbacks: Faulty steering sensor does not impact camera operation.
Misaligned radar sensor does not impact lane centering.
Camera's can have their visibility reduced in low light.
Low battery voltage has no direct impact on lane assist.
questions.explanation: LKA uses a camera to see lane markings therefore poor camera visibility reduces its effectiveness.

questions.question: A vehicle's all-wheel-drive (AWD) system is experiencing a binding sensation during low-speed turns. What could be a likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires dont cause binding sensation during low speed turns.
Worn wheel bearings don't cause binding.
Incorrect or contaminated differential fluid can cause a binding sensation during low speed turns.
Loose suspension components wont cause binding.
questions.explanation: Incorrect or contaminated differential fluid will cause binding in the differential when turning at low speeds.

questions.question: A vehicle's brake system is exhibiting a 'spongy' feel. What is a likely mechanical cause?
feedbacks: Worn brake pads dont cause a spongy feel.
Air in the brake lines will cause a 'spongy' feel in the brake pedal.
Worn tires do not cause a spongy feel.
Overheated brake rotors will cause brake fade.
questions.explanation: Air in the brake lines introduces a compressible fluid and will result in a spongy pedal feel.

questions.question: An engine is experiencing excessive oil consumption. Which of the following is the most likely reason?
feedbacks: Clogged air filter can cause a rich condition.
Worn piston rings are a major cause for excessive oil consumption.
Leaking radiator does not relate to oil consumption.
Faulty O2 sensor does not affect oil consumption.
questions.explanation: Worn piston rings will allow engine oil to leak into the combustion chamber and cause oil consumption.

questions.question: A hybrid vehicle's regenerative braking system is showing inconsistent performance. What could be a cause?
feedbacks: Faulty ABS sensors do not relate to regenerative braking performance.
Worn brake pads do not impact regenerative braking performance.
Inconsistent battery state of charge is a common reason for inconsistent regen braking.
Overheated engine coolant has no impact on regen braking.
questions.explanation: Regenerative braking relies on consistent battery state of charge, inconsistencies will reduce its effectiveness.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive headlight system is failing to adjust properly during cornering. Which sensor is crucial?
feedbacks: Frontal impact sensors do not correlate with adaptive headlights.
Steering angle sensors provide the direction for the headlights to follow.

Worn brake pads will reduce overall braking performance.
questions.explanation: A faulty wheel speed sensor on one side of the car will cause that wheel's ABS to stop working completely, while the other wheels will continue to modulate and will illuminate the warning light.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a consistent lack of power, poor fuel economy, rough idle, frequent misfires, a strong smell of unburnt fuel and the check engine light is illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Clogged air filters cause a rich condition.
Leaking intake gaskets cause a lean condition.
Faulty injectors cause poor economy, misfires and rough idle.
Worn spark plugs can cause misfires.
questions.explanation: Both faulty fuel injectors and worn spark plugs will create various issues including poor fuel economy, misfires, rough idle and a fuel smell. Either of these can illuminate a check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is exhibiting a tendency to consistently fail to recognize vehicles ahead in poor weather conditions such as heavy rain or snow. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Poor radar visibility due to adverse weather
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not manage object detection.
Misaligned radar sensors can create reduced performance.
Dirty radar sensors can create reduced performance.
Poor weather conditions will limit the ability for the system to function.
questions.explanation: Both dirty radar sensors and poor weather conditions will severely limit the ability of the system to detect vehicles ahead and perform properly.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is exhibiting completely incorrect pressure readings, and the system warning light is always on and all sensors are known to be good. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Faulty TPMS receiver module or antenna
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to TPMS functionality.
Radar sensors do not relate to TPMS functionality.
Low battery voltage can create incorrect readings.
Faulty receivers will give incorrect readings from the system.
questions.explanation: A faulty receiver module or antenna will prevent the system from correctly reading data from the TPMS sensors and can cause incorrect pressure readings, and illuminate the warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is exhibiting a complete lack of cooling, reduced airflow, and a constant hissing noise that is coming from the engine bay. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Faulty A/C compressor clutch or control
feedbacks: Cabin filters do not cause a hissing sound.
Low refrigerant can cause a hiss.
Faulty compressors do not cause hissing.
Leaking A/C lines will cause a hissing sound.
questions.explanation: Both low refrigerant levels, and leaks in the lines or condenser will cause reduced cooling, airflow, and a hissing sound in the engine bay.

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery pack is exhibiting a significantly reduced range, frequent cell voltage imbalances and an accelerated rate of self discharge when left unused. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Slow charging does not relate to these issues.
Internal cell damage will cause all 3 issues.
Overcharging does not cause self discharge or imbalance.
Ideal conditions do not degrade battery performance.
questions.explanation: Internal cell damage or shorts will cause reduced range, imbalanced cell voltages, and a high rate of self discharge.

questions.question: A vehicle's limited-slip differential (LSD) is experiencing a consistent 'clunking' noise and binding sensation that is present during tight, low-speed turns on dry pavement. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause binding or clunking in the LSD.
Low differential fluid will cause whining.
Worn components create clunking and binding.
Overheated rotors do not impact differential operation.
questions.explanation: Worn components in the LSD will cause a clunking sound and will prevent the LSD from operating properly, creating a binding sensation during low speed turns.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is exhibiting a complete lack of functionality, with a warning message on the dashboard that states 'Camera Obstructed' or 'System Unavailable'. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Obstructed camera view or faulty connection
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to lane keeping.
Radar sensors do not manage the LKA system.
Obstructed view or faulty camera connection will prevent operation.
Low battery voltage does not relate to the camera system.
questions.explanation: A camera obstruction or faulty connection will prevent the LKA system from working, and will illuminate a message on the dashboard.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is exhibiting a complete loss of assist, but only after extended periods of highway driving and then becomes difficult to steer during low-speed maneuvers. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause this.
Low fluid creates heavy steering not a complete loss.
Failing pumps will fail during extended use and low speeds.
Misaligned steering does not cause steering assist issues.
questions.explanation: A failing power steering pump will not have the ability to provide adequate assist after extended periods of use, and will cause a loss of power during low speed maneuvers.

questions.question: A vehicle's differential is experiencing a consistent 'humming' noise that is most prominent during highway driving, and will disappear during deceleration. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not relate to differential noises.
Low differential fluid will not create a highway specific humming sound.
Worn gears do not create a humming sound.
Damaged bearings will create a humming noise at highway speed.
questions.explanation: Damaged pinion gear bearings will create a humming sound during highway driving, but it will disappear when decelerating due to reduced load.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is exhibiting an inconsistent response, sometimes activating too early, and sometimes too late, and a system warning light illuminates intermittently. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn brake pads do not cause an inconsistent response.
Faulty yaw rate sensors cause inconsistent responses.
Misaligned steering does not cause inconsistent ESC.
Low tire pressure does not cause inconsistent response from ESC.
questions.explanation: A faulty yaw rate sensor will cause the system to have an inconsistent and delayed response, and can cause the system warning light to illuminate intermittently.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is exhibiting a complete failure on all wheels, and also causes a reduction in the braking performance of all wheels, and the warning light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to ABS.
Radar sensors do not relate to braking.
A faulty control module will cause full failure.
Worn brake pads will reduce braking performance.
questions.explanation: A faulty ABS control module will cause a complete failure of the system and will also illuminate the warning light and prevent the system from modulating pressure which will reduce braking performance.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a complete lack of power, very rough idle, and frequent stalling, a strong smell of unburnt fuel and excessive black smoke from the exhaust and the check engine light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Clogged air filters create rich conditions.
Leaking intake gaskets cause lean conditions.
Faulty fuel injectors cause all of the mentioned symptoms.
Worn spark plugs do not cause all of these symptoms.
questions.explanation: Faulty fuel injectors can cause all the mentioned issues including a complete lack of power, rough idling, frequent stalling, fuel smells and excessive black smoke, and will also illuminate the check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is exhibiting a tendency to inconsistently adjust the speed, surging and slowing, and overreacting to small changes in the distance to the vehicle ahead and the warning light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not impact speed control.
Misaligned sensors create inconsistent speed adjustments.
Dirty sensors create inconsistent speed adjustments.
Faulty control modules create inconsistent adjustments.
questions.explanation: A misaligned or dirty sensor or a faulty control module can cause inconsistent operation that includes surging and slowing and over reacting to distance changes and will also illuminate the warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is exhibiting completely incorrect and very inconsistent pressure readings with some sensors showing very high pressure, and others showing extremely low pressure, and the warning light is on. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Faulty TPMS sensor in the wheel
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to TPMS.
Radar sensors do not relate to TPMS.
Low battery voltage will not cause high or low readings.
Faulty sensors cause inconsistent and incorrect data.
questions.explanation: A faulty sensor in one or more tires will cause the system to report incorrect data, and cause inconsistent readings with some reading high and some low and also will illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is exhibiting a complete lack of cooling, reduced airflow, a burning plastic or electrical odor, and a consistent loud squealing sound from the compressor. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Blocked expansion valve or orifice tube
feedbacks: Cabin filters do not cause electrical or squealing noises.
Low refrigerant does not cause electrical odors.
Faulty compressors can produce all these symptoms.
A blocked valve or tube does not cause electrical smells or squealing.
questions.explanation: A faulty A/C compressor will not be able to create cooling, will cause a reduction in airflow, will make a squealing sound and when faulty can create a burning plastic odor.

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery pack is exhibiting a significantly reduced range, significantly reduced charging rate and is producing excessive heat during normal driving and when charging. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Internal cell degradation and increased resistance
feedbacks: Slow charging will not cause all these issues.
Increased resistance will cause these symptoms.
Overcharging degrades the cells not cause these specific issues.
Ideal conditions do not cause degradation or overheating.
questions.explanation: Internal cell degradation increases resistance and will cause a reduced range, slow charging speeds and excessive heat generation, especially during driving and charging.

questions.question: A vehicle's limited-slip differential (LSD) is experiencing a loud and consistent 'grinding' noise, a binding sensation, and reduced effectiveness when turning on dry pavement, especially when accelerating. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Worn LSD clutch packs or gears
feedbacks: Worn tires do not create a grinding sound in the LSD.
Low differential fluid will cause a whining.
Worn components can create grinding and binding during operation.
Overheated rotors do not impact the LSD system.
questions.explanation: Worn components in the LSD will not engage properly and will create grinding noises, a binding sensation, and a reduction in its ability to transfer power, especially when accelerating and turning on dry pavement.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is exhibiting erratic behavior, frequently activating when there are no lane markings and also sometimes not activating when it is required to, with a system warning light that will intermittently illuminate. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not impact lane keep behavior.
Radar sensors do not manage the LKA system.
A faulty camera or connection causes erratic operation.
Low battery voltage will not cause erratic operation of LKA.
questions.explanation: A faulty camera sensor or connection will cause the system to operate erratically and sometimes not at all, and will cause an intermittent system warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is exhibiting a complete loss of assist only when turning to one side, and also accompanied by a grinding noise during turns. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause one sided steering issues.
Low fluid creates heavy steering.
Faulty rack will cause binding and grinding.
Misaligned steering causes pulling not power assist issues.
questions.explanation: A faulty steering rack will not operate properly and will cause a complete loss of assist only when turning one direction and may also create grinding noises during operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's differential is experiencing a consistent 'humming' noise that is most noticeable during acceleration and deceleration, and will completely disappear during consistent cruising speeds. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause differential humming.
Low differential fluid will cause whining not humming.
Worn gears do not create a humming noise.
Damaged bearings cause humming that disappears at cruise.
questions.explanation: Damaged pinion gear bearings will create a humming noise that will be most noticeable during acceleration and deceleration, but will disappear during consistent cruising speeds due to the constant load and rotation.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is exhibiting inconsistent and delayed activation, sometimes engaging correctly but other times either too late or not at all, and a system warning light illuminates intermittently. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn brake pads do not cause inconsistent activation.
Faulty yaw rate sensors will cause inconsistent and delayed activation.
Misaligned steering does not impact the ESC response time.
Low tire pressure does not impact the system response time.
questions.explanation: A faulty yaw rate sensor will cause the system to have erratic and delayed responses and can cause the system warning light to illuminate intermittently.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is exhibiting a complete failure and also is causing a complete lack of braking performance on all wheels with the system warning light illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to ABS functionality.
Radar sensors do not relate to ABS functionality.
A faulty ABS control module will cause a full system failure.
Worn brake pads will reduce overall braking performance not prevent it completely.
questions.explanation: A faulty ABS control module will prevent the entire system from functioning, and will also prevent braking functionality as well as illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a complete lack of power, frequent stalling, rough idle, no acceleration above idle, a strong fuel smell, and black smoke, and the check engine light is illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Clogged air filters cause a rich condition.
Leaking intake manifold gaskets cause a lean condition.
Faulty fuel injectors cause a rich condition, stalling, no RPMs, fuel smell and black smoke.
Worn spark plugs cause misfires.
questions.explanation: Faulty fuel injectors can cause all of these symptoms, including a lack of power, stalling, rough idles, a fuel smell, and black smoke, and will also illuminate the check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is exhibiting erratic and unsafe behavior, including a tendency to rapidly accelerate then suddenly and aggressively brake, and also frequently losing track of the vehicle ahead and the system warning light is on. What is a MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not impact ACC acceleration.
Misaligned radar sensors cause erratic performance.
Dirty radar sensors cause reduced performance.
A faulty control module can cause all these issues.
questions.explanation: A misaligned or dirty sensor, or a faulty control module can cause a variety of unsafe behavior patterns, including sudden accelerations and decelerations, losing track of vehicles ahead, and illuminate the warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is exhibiting completely incorrect and unreliable data with no sensors registering correctly, and a consistent warning light that remains on at all times, and is also not communicating with the vehicles onboard computer. What is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to TPMS operation.
Radar sensors do not relate to TPMS operation.
Low battery voltage can reduce sensor performance.
A faulty receiver will prevent communication to the computer.
questions.explanation: A faulty TPMS receiver module will prevent the entire system from operating, will cause completely incorrect data, will illuminate the warning light and will also prevent the computer from communicating with the system.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is exhibiting a complete lack of cooling, airflow, all components not operating, a persistent burning electrical smell, and also a rattling sound coming from under the dashboard. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Faulty A/C compressor clutch or control
Faulty blower motor resistor or module
feedbacks: Cabin filters do not cause a lack of cooling, airflow, electrical odors and rattling.
Low refrigerant will not prevent system engagement or cause electrical odors and rattling.
A faulty compressor will not produce all the listed symptoms.
Faulty blower controls can cause a lack of airflow, electrical odors, and the rattling sounds.
questions.explanation: A faulty blower motor control module or resistor will prevent airflow from occurring, it can create a burning electrical smell, and also can create a rattling sound, but will not prevent the compressor from working.

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery pack is exhibiting an extremely rapid decrease in driving range, very slow charging times, a rapid and consistent increase in temperature during charging and normal driving, frequent and severe cell voltage imbalances and also exhibits signs of rapid swelling in the pack. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Internal cell short circuits and damage
feedbacks: Slow charging does not cause any of these issues.
Internal cell shorts cause all of the issues mentioned.
Overcharging does not create swelling or cell imbalance.
Ideal conditions do not cause any degradation in performance.
questions.explanation: Internal cell shorts will cause a rapid loss in range, a significantly reduced charging rate, high temperatures, cell voltage imbalances and rapid swelling due to out gassing.

questions.question: A vehicle's limited-slip differential (LSD) is exhibiting a consistent 'grinding' noise, significant binding during turns, frequent clicking or popping noises and a reduction in performance when accelerating on loose surfaces. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Severely worn or damaged LSD clutch packs and gears
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause LSD issues.
Low differential fluid causes whining.
Worn or damaged components will cause all the mentioned symptoms.
Overheated rotors do not impact the LSD.
questions.explanation: Severely worn or damaged LSD components including gears and clutch packs will cause significant issues during normal operation, including grinding, binding, clicking or popping noises, and a significant reduction in performance especially on low grip surfaces.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane keep assist (LKA) system is exhibiting a complete lack of functionality with the warning message 'System Unavailable, Steering Assistance Disabled', a warning light on the dashboard, and the system failing to activate even when lane markings are clearly visible. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the camera and its associated wiring and control systems
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not prevent system operation.
Radar sensors do not relate to lane keeping systems.
Complete camera failure or wiring issues will cause a system failure.
Low battery voltage does not cause a complete system failure.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the camera and its associated wiring or control systems will cause the system to completely fail and illuminate the warning message.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is exhibiting a complete loss of power assist, a loud grinding noise, significant stiffness in the steering, and also a noticeable resistance when turning the wheel, only when turning to one side, and especially noticeable during parking maneuvers. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the steering rack internals
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause the listed issues.
Low power steering fluid will cause heavy steering.
A rack failure will cause all the mentioned issues.
Misaligned steering will not cause all the mentioned issues.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the steering rack internals will not operate correctly and will result in a complete loss of assist when turning to only one side, will create a grinding noise, and significant resistance, especially during low speed operation and parking maneuvers.

questions.question: A vehicle's differential is exhibiting a consistent 'whining' noise during operation, which will rapidly become a 'howling' noise during acceleration, and a consistent 'grinding' noise during deceleration, and will also exhibit a clunking noise when turning sharply, and is producing metallic flakes in the differential fluid when changed. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Severe damage to the differential gears and bearings
feedbacks: Worn tires do not relate to differential noises.
Low differential fluid will not cause all the listed symptoms.
Severely worn gears and bearings will cause all of the listed issues.
Overheated rotors do not relate to the differential.
questions.explanation: Severe damage to the differential gears and bearings will cause a variety of issues including whining noises during normal operation, howling during acceleration, grinding during deceleration, clunking when turning, and will also produce metallic flakes in the fluid due to the material breaking down.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is exhibiting a complete lack of activation, a system warning light that is constantly on, a noticeable pulling sensation towards one side when cornering and a reduction in braking effectiveness of only one side of the vehicle. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: A complete failure of the ABS and Yaw Rate Sensor
feedbacks: Worn brake pads will only reduce braking performance not cause system failure.
Faulty yaw rate sensors do not cause only one side to perform poorly.
Complete system failure will cause the issues mentioned.
Low tire pressure does not relate to complete system failure.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the ABS and Yaw Rate sensors will prevent proper stability control operation and will result in a complete failure of the ESC system, including a pull to one side during cornering due to uneven braking and will illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is exhibiting a complete failure, along with a complete lack of braking on all wheels, a system warning light is on, a complete lack of engagement of the EBD system and a noticeable pulling sensation to one side, and the vehicle will not start with the ABS system connected. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the ABS Control Module
feedbacks: Steering sensors do not relate to braking performance.
Radar sensors do not relate to braking performance.
A faulty ABS control module causes a complete system failure.
Worn brake pads do not prevent the system from working.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the ABS control module will prevent all of the system operations, and will also cause the entire system to be inoperable, which will also cause a lack of braking, and will prevent the car from starting and illuminate the system warning light.

questions.question: A gasoline engine is exhibiting a complete lack of power, frequent stalling, a very rough idle, a strong smell of unburnt fuel, significant black smoke, and also a loud backfiring sound when the engine is turned off and a check engine light is illuminated. What is a MOST likely cause?
answers: Complete failure of the fuel injection system
feedbacks: Clogged air filters cause a rich condition.
Leaking intake gaskets cause a lean condition.
A complete failure will cause all of the listed symptoms.
Worn spark plugs cause misfires.
questions.explanation: A complete failure of the fuel injection system will cause all of the listed symptoms including a lack of power, frequent stalling, a rough idle, a strong fuel smell, black smoke, and also backfiring, and will illuminate the check engine light.

questions.question: A vehicle's adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is experiencing frequent and unwarranted braking events on curved roads. This is most likely due to a failure in which system?
feedbacks: Radar sensors primarily detect distance and speed, not curvature.
Lidar sensors are used for high definition mapping and object detection but not specifically curvature
Steering angle sensors provide information about steering wheel position but does not infer road curvature
Lateral acceleration sensors measure the force experienced during turning, allowing the system to differentiate a turn versus a possible accident.
questions.explanation: Lateral acceleration sensors are the most likely culprit when ACC causes frequent braking events on curved roads because it measures force experienced during a turn allowing the system to differenciate a turn from a possible accident

questions.question: An electric vehicle's battery management system (BMS) is reporting an imbalance in cell voltages during charging. What could be a potential cause for this?
feedbacks: A faulty charger would cause issues in the whole charging system not specifically cell imbalance.
Temperature variation between cells can lead to internal resistance differences, therefore causing cell imbalance.
Coolant is important for thermal management, not cell imbalance.
Overcharging can cause multiple failures but not specifically cell voltage imbalance.
questions.explanation: Temperature differences create variance in cell internal resistance, resulting in imbalance of voltages.

questions.question: A gasoline engine experiences significant pre-ignition (knock). Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: Low octane fuel causes detonation not pre-ignition.
Rich air-fuel mixture will not cause pre-ignition.
Excessive spark advance is a primary cause of pre-ignition.
Leaking intake valve would not cause pre-ignition
questions.explanation: Excessive spark advance causes the mixture to ignite too early, creating knock.

questions.question: During a crash test, a vehicle's side impact airbags fail to deploy. Which sensor is MOST crucial for proper side airbag deployment?
feedbacks: Frontal impact sensors activate the frontal airbags.
Side impact pressure sensors are designed to activate side airbags on impact.
Yaw rate sensors measure rotation but are not necessary for side airbag deployment.
Wheel speed sensors measure rotational speed.
questions.explanation: Side impact pressure sensors are placed in the doors and side structures to detect an impact and trigger the side airbag.

questions.question: A vehicle's CAN bus is experiencing intermittent communication errors. What is a common cause of such an issue?
feedbacks: Low battery voltage causes various problems, but specifically intermittent CAN bus issues.
Incorrect CAN bus termination resistors are common causes of intermittent CAN bus communication.
Faulty ECU can cause various issues but not specifically intermittent CAN bus errors.
Overheated Transmission Control Module would cause Transmission specific errors not CAN bus errors.
questions.explanation: Improper CAN bus termination resistors will create signal reflection that leads to communication errors.

questions.question: A vehicle's steering system exhibits excessive play (looseness). What is a likely mechanical cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires do not cause steering play.
Tie rod ends connect steering to the wheels, and when loose will result in excessive play.
Worn brake rotors do not cause steering play.
Incorrect wheel alignment can cause handling issues, not steering play.
questions.explanation: Loose tie rod ends will result in a loose or undefined feel to the steering response.

questions.question: A vehicle's hybrid system is showing reduced regenerative braking efficiency. Which component is the MOST likely source of the problem?
feedbacks: Inverter changes DC to AC, not a likely cause of reduced regen.
Battery packs hold the charge, so reduced efficiency is not a cause.
The electric motor is responsible for both generating and propulsion, so this is the most likely cause.
Transmission transmits mechanical power and would not affect regenerative braking.
questions.explanation: The electric motor generator is responsible for both propulsion and regenerative braking, and is most likely the cause when regen efficiency is reduced.

questions.question: A vehicle with a direct injection gasoline engine is experiencing carbon buildup on the intake valves. Which is the most effective solution?
feedbacks: Fuel system cleaner does not clean the intake valves in DI engines.
Direct mechanical cleaning of the intake valves is the most effective solution.
High octane fuel does not mitigate the cause of carbon buildup.
Engine oil additives do not remove carbon buildup on intake valves.
questions.explanation: Direct injection does not allow fuel/cleaner to clean the intake valves, therefore a cleaning service is required.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is activating excessively, even during normal driving. What could be a potential cause?
feedbacks: Incorrect tire pressure can cause vehicle instability and trigger ESC.
Faulty wheel speed sensors can provide inaccurate data, causing ESC to trigger even if it is not needed.
Worn brake pads don't cause ESC issues.
Engine misfires will not cause ESC issues.
questions.explanation: Faulty wheel speed sensors would provide inaccurate data causing ESC to activate without needing to.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic transmission is experiencing rough shifts and slippage. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Worn clutch plates in the differential
feedbacks: Worn engine mounts cause engine vibrations, not transmission slippage.
Low transmission fluid level will cause rough shifts and slippage.
Faulty ABS sensors do not cause transmission issues.
Differential does not cause transmission issues.
questions.explanation: Low transmission fluid will prevent adequate pressure and lubrication, which leads to slippage and rough shifts.

questions.question: A vehicle's radar-based blind spot monitoring system is giving false alarms, particularly in heavy rain. What is the most likely cause?
answers: Radar sensor is being blocked by debris
Signal reflection due to heavy rain
feedbacks: While faulty radar sensor is a possibility, rain can cause issues with radar based systems
Misaligned radar sensors will not cause false alarms only in heavy rain.
Debris would cause false alarms at all times, not just in the rain
Heavy rain can reflect radar signals, causing the system to falsely detect objects.
questions.explanation: Heavy rain will create signal reflection that can lead to the radar sensing multiple non existent objects.

questions.question: A vehicle's thermal management system for the battery pack is experiencing reduced performance. Which component is the MOST likely source of the problem?
feedbacks: Coolant pumps keep the coolant flow moving. Faulty pumps would reduce performance.
Cabin heater does not manage battery pack temperature.
HVAC compressor does not manage battery pack temperature.
Battery control module monitors, not manage temperature directly.
questions.explanation: Coolant pumps move the coolant that transfers heat from the battery to the radiator, a faulty pump would cause reduced performance.

questions.question: A high-performance vehicle exhibits excessive understeer during cornering. What is the MOST likely cause related to chassis setup?
feedbacks: Stiff rear sway bar promotes oversteer.
Stiff front sway bar will cause excessive understeer.
High rear tire pressure promotes oversteer.
Low front tire pressure promotes oversteer.
questions.explanation: Stiff front sway bar transfers more load to the front, making the front tires lose grip and therefore promoting understeer.

questions.question: A diesel engine is emitting excessive black smoke. What is the most likely reason?
feedbacks: Exhaust manifold leaks would not cause black smoke.
Faulty injectors will cause overfueling which leads to black smoke.
Clogged air filters cause a lean condition, and not black smoke.
Low compression does not cause black smoke.
questions.explanation: Faulty injectors can cause overfueling which leads to excess unburnt fuel.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is activating erratically during normal braking. Which sensor could be the cause?
feedbacks: Steering angle sensor provides data for steering, not braking.
Brake pressure sensor does not directly control ABS activation.
Erratic wheel speed sensors will cause ABS to engage when unnecessary.
Yaw rate sensor measure rotation, not braking.
questions.explanation: Erratic wheel speed sensor data will cause the ABS system to think the wheels are locking up when they are not.

questions.question: A vehicle's transmission control module (TCM) is reporting a solenoid fault code. What is the function of solenoids in an automatic transmission?
feedbacks: Solenoids don't measure fluid temp.
Solenoids are electrical valves that direct hydraulic pressure, therefore control gear shifting.
Solenoids don't control engine timing.
Solenoids don't regulate brake force.
questions.explanation: Solenoids are used in automatic transmissions to control gear shifting by controlling the flow of hydraulic pressure to clutches or brakes inside the transmission.

questions.question: A vehicle's electric power steering (EPS) system is becoming stiff or difficult to turn intermittently. Which could be a potential cause?
answers: Weak electrical connection to the EPS motor
feedbacks: Low tire pressure can cause difficulty in steering but not intermittent.
A faulty steering sensor would not cause stiffness, rather no steering.
A weak electrical connection can cause intermittent stiffness in electric power steering.
Worn steering rack will cause play or looseness, not intermittent stiffness.
questions.explanation: A poor electrical connection causes the EPS system to intermittently stop working or not operate at 100%.

questions.question: A vehicle with a continuously variable transmission (CVT) is experiencing belt slippage. Which is a potential mechanical reason?
answers: Worn clutch pack in the differential
feedbacks: Worn engine mounts don't cause slippage.
Low transmission fluid causes slippage in all types of transmissions.
Overheated brake rotors do not cause transmission slippage.
Differential does not cause CVT slippage.
questions.explanation: Low transmission fluid causes a lack of hydraulic pressure on the belt resulting in slippage.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane departure warning (LDW) system is frequently triggered on straight roads, even when the vehicle is centered in the lane. What could be the most likely cause?
feedbacks: Steering sensors measure steering input not vehicle position in a lane
Misaligned camera sensor or poor calibration will cause the LDW to malfunction.
Incorrect tire pressure has no direct correlation with lane assist.
Weak battery has no direct correlation with lane assist
questions.explanation: Misaligned camera sensors or poor calibration will give the LDW a false view of the lane markings.

questions.question: A vehicle's active suspension system is exhibiting inconsistent damping performance. What could be the most likely cause?
feedbacks: Worn tires don't affect damping.
Faulty air compressor does not affect damping specifically.
Faulty damping actuators directly affect damping by controlling the valve within the shock.
Misaligned steering does not affect damping.
questions.explanation: Damping actuators control the valves within the shock to vary damping force.

questions.question: A lithium-ion battery pack is experiencing rapid capacity degradation. What is the MOST likely cause related to charging behavior?
feedbacks: Slow charging is typically good for battery health.
